q: What did the prophet Isaiah predict would happen before the Lord came?
a: Isaiah predicted that God would send a messenger, a voice of someone calling out in the wilderness, to prepare the way of the Lord.

q: What did John come preaching?
a: John came preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.

q: What did the people do as they were baptized by John?
a: The people confessed their sins as they were baptized by John.

q: What did John eat?
a: John ate locusts and wild honey.

q: With what did John say the one coming after him would baptize?
a: John said the one coming after him would baptize with the Holy Spirit.

q: What did Jesus see as he came up out of the water after being baptized by John?
a: After being baptized, Jesus saw the heavens split open and the Spirit descend on him as a dove.

q: What did the voice from heaven say after Jesus was baptized?
a: The voice from heaven said, “You are my beloved Son; I am very pleased with you.”

q: Who drove Jesus out into the wilderness?
a: The Spirit drove Jesus out into the wilderness.

q: How long was Jesus in the wilderness, and what happened to him there?
a: Jesus was in the wilderness 40 days, and he was tempted by Satan there.

q: What message did Jesus preach?
a: Jesus preached that the kingdom of God was near, and that people must repent and believe in the gospel.

q: What was the occupation of Simon and Andrew?
a: Simon and Andrew were fishermen.

q: What did Jesus say he would make Simon and Andrew become?
a: Jesus said he would make Simon and Andrew fishers of men.

q: What was the occupation of James and John?
a: James and John were fishermen.

q: Why did Jesus’ teaching astonish the people in the synagogue?
a: Jesus’ teaching astonished the people because Jesus taught as one with authority.

q: What title did the unclean spirit in the synagogue give Jesus?
a: The unclean spirit in the synagogue gave Jesus the title of the Holy One of God.

q: What happened with the news about Jesus?
a: The news about Jesus went out everywhere.

q: When they went into Simon’s house, who did Jesus heal?
a: When they went into Simon’s house, Jesus healed Simon’s mother-in-law.

q: What happened when it was evening?
a: When it was evening, the people brought all who were sick or possessed by demons, and Jesus healed them.

q: What did Jesus do before the sun rose?
a: Before the sun rose, Jesus went out to a solitary place and prayed there.

q: What did Jesus tell Simon he had come to do?
a: Jesus said that he had come to preach in the surrounding towns.

q: What attitude did Jesus have toward the leper who begged Jesus to be healed?
a: Jesus had pity on the leper and healed him.

q: What did Jesus tell the leper to do, and why?
a: Jesus told the leper to go offer the sacrifices according to what Moses commanded. It would serve the community as a testimony that he was healed.

q: What did the four men do who were carrying the paralyzed man?
a: The men removed the roof of the house and lowered the paralyzed man to Jesus.

q: What did Jesus say to the paralyzed man?
a: Jesus said, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”

q: Why did some of the scribes object to what Jesus had said?
a: Some of the scribes reasoned that Jesus had blasphemed because only God can forgive sins.

q: How did Jesus demonstrate that he had authority on earth to forgive sins?
a: Jesus told the paralyzed man to take up his bed and go to his house, and the man did.

q: What was Levi doing when Jesus told Levi to follow him?
a: Levi was sitting at the tax-collecting place when Jesus called him.

q: At Levi’s house, what was Jesus doing that offended the Pharisees?
a: Jesus was dining with the sinful people and tax collectors.

q: Who did Jesus say he had come to call?
a: Jesus said he had come to call sinful people.

q: What question did some people ask Jesus about fasting?
a: They asked Jesus why his disciples did not fast when John’s disciples and the Pharisees’ disciples did fast.

q: How did Jesus explain why his disciples were not fasting?
a: Jesus said that while the bridegroom is still with the wedding attendants, they cannot fast.

q: What did Jesus’ disciples do in some fields on the Sabbath which offended the Pharisees?
a: Jesus’ disciples picked heads of grain and ate them on the Sabbath.

q: What example did Jesus give of someone who needed and ate bread normally forbidden for them?
a: Jesus gave the example of David who, out of need, ate the bread of the presence, normally reserved for the priests.

q: For whom did Jesus say the Sabbath was made?
a: Jesus said the Sabbath was made for people.

q: What authority did Jesus claim for himself?
a: Jesus said that he was Lord also of the Sabbath.

q: Why were they watching Jesus on the Sabbath in the synagogue?
a: They were watching Jesus to see if he would heal on the Sabbath, so they could accuse him.

q: What question did Jesus ask the people about the Sabbath?
a: Jesus asked the people if it was lawful to do good, or to do harm on the Sabbath.

q: How did the people respond to Jesus’ question?
a: The people were silent.

q: What then was Jesus’ attitude toward them?
a: Jesus became angry with them.

q: What did the Pharisees do when Jesus healed the man?
a: The Pharisees went out and plotted to put Jesus to death.

q: How many people followed Jesus as he went to the sea?
a: A great crowd followed Jesus.

q: What did the demons cry out when they saw Jesus?
a: The demons cried out that Jesus was the Son of God.

q: How many men did Jesus appoint as apostles, and what were they to do?
a: Jesus appointed 12 apostles who were to be with him, preach, and have authority to cast out demons.

q: Who was the apostle that would betray Jesus?
a: The apostle that would betray Jesus was Judas Iscariot.

q: What did Jesus’ family think about the crowds and the events surrounding Jesus?
a: Jesus’ family thought that he was out of his mind.

q: What accusation did the scribes make against Jesus?
a: The scribes accused Jesus of driving out demons by the ruler of demons.

q: What was Jesus’ response to the scribes’ accusation?
a: Jesus responded that no kingdom divided against itself can stand.

q: What sin did Jesus say cannot be forgiven?
a: Jesus said that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit cannot be forgiven.

q: Who did Jesus say were his mother and brothers?
a: Jesus said that his mother and brothers were those who do the will of God.

q: Why did Jesus get into a boat to teach?
a: Jesus got into a boat to sit and teach because a very large crowd had gathered around him.

q: What happened to the seeds sown on the road?
a: The birds came and devoured them.

q: What happened to the seeds sown on the rocky ground when the sun rose?
a: They withered away because they had no root.

q: What happened to the seeds sown among thorn plants?
a: The thorn plants choked them.

q: What happened to the seeds sown in the good soil?
a: The seeds produced grain, yielding 30, 60, and some, 100 times what was planted.

q: What did Jesus say was given to the Twelve, but not to those outside?
a: Jesus said the mystery of the kingdom of God was given to the Twelve, but not to those outside.

q: In Jesus’ parable, what is the seed?
a: The seed is the word of God.

q: What does the seed sown on the road represent?
a: It represents those who hear the word, but immediately Satan takes it away.

q: What does the seed sown on the rocky ground represent?
a: It represents those who hear the word with joy, but when persecution comes, they stumble.

q: What does the seed sown among thorn plants represent?
a: It represents those who hear the word, but the cares of the world choke the word.

q: What does the seed sown in the good soil represent?
a: It represents those who hear the word, receive it, and produce fruit.

q: What did Jesus say would happen to the hidden and secret things?
a: Jesus said that the hidden and secret things would be brought into the light.

q: In what way is the kingdom of God like a man who casts his seed upon the ground?
a: The man casts the seed, and it grows, but he does not know how, then when the harvest is ripe he gathers it.

q: In what way is the kingdom of God like a mustard seed?
a: The mustard seed begins as the smallest of seeds, yet grows into a great plant where many can make their nests.

q: What happened as the disciples and Jesus crossed the lake?
a: A great storm began, threatening to fill the boat with water.

q: What was Jesus doing at this time in the boat?
a: Jesus was sleeping.

q: What question did the disciples ask Jesus?
a: The disciples asked Jesus if he cared that they were about to die.

q: What did Jesus then do?
a: Jesus rebuked the wind and calmed the sea.

q: After Jesus did this, what was the response of the disciples?
a: The disciples were filled with great fear and wondered who Jesus was, that the wind and sea obeyed him.

q: Who met Jesus when they came to the region of the Gerasenes?
a: A man with an unclean spirit met Jesus.

q: What had happened when people tried to restrain this man with chains?
a: When people tried to restrain this man with chains, he tore the chains apart.

q: What title did the unclean spirit give Jesus?
a: The unclean spirit called Jesus the Son of the Most High God.

q: What did Jesus say to the unclean spirit in the man?
a: Jesus said, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit.”

q: What was the name of the unclean spirit?
a: The unclean spirit’s name was Legion, because there were many.

q: What happened when Jesus cast out the unclean spirit from the man?
a: The spirits came out and entered a herd of pigs, which ran down a steep hill and drowned in the lake.

q: After the unclean spirit was cast out, what was the condition of the man?
a: The man was sitting with Jesus, clothed and in his right mind.

q: What did the people of the region ask Jesus to do?
a: The people asked Jesus to leave their region.

q: What did Jesus tell the man who had lived in the tombs to now do?
a: Jesus told the man to tell his people what the Lord had done for him.

q: What request did Jairus, the synagogue leader, make of Jesus?
a: Jairus asked Jesus to come with him to lay hands on his daughter, who was near death.

q: What was the problem with the woman who touched Jesus’ cloak?
a: The woman had suffered with a discharge of blood for 12 years.

q: Why did the woman touch Jesus’ cloak?
a: The woman thought that if she just touched Jesus’ clothes, she would be healed.

q: What did Jesus do when the woman touched his cloak?
a: Jesus knew that power had gone out from him so he asked who touched his clothes.

q: What did Jesus do after the woman touched his cloak?
a: Jesus looked around to see who had touched him.

q: When the woman told Jesus all the truth, what did Jesus say to her?
a: Jesus told her that her faith had made her well, and to go in peace.

q: What was the condition of Jairus’ daughter when Jesus arrived at the house?
a: Jairus’ daughter was dead.

q: What did Jesus tell Jairus at this time?
a: Jesus told Jairus to not be afraid, but to just believe.

q: Which disciples went with Jesus into the room where the child was?
a: Peter, James, and John went with Jesus into the room.

q: What did the people in the house do when Jesus said Jairus’ daughter was only sleeping?
a: The people laughed at Jesus when he said that Jairus’ daughter was only sleeping.

q: When the child got up and walked, how did the people react?
a: The people were greatly overcome and astonished.

q: Why were the people of Jesus’ home town shocked about him?
a: The people did not know from where he got his teachings, his wisdom, and his miracles.

q: Where did Jesus say a prophet is without honor?
a: Jesus said a prophet is without honor in his home town, among his relatives, and in his own household.

q: What amazed Jesus about the people in his home town?
a: Jesus was amazed by the unbelief of the people in his home town.

q: What authority did Jesus give the Twelve as he sent them out?
a: Jesus gave the Twelve authority over unclean spirits.

q: What did the Twelve take with them on their journey?
a: The Twelve took a staff, sandals, and one tunic.

q: What did Jesus tell the Twelve to do if a place did not receive them?
a: Jesus told the Twelve to shake off the dust under their feet as a testimony against them.

q: Who did the people suppose Jesus was?
a: The people supposed that Jesus was John the Baptizer or Elijah or a prophet.

q: What had John the Baptizer told Herod he was doing unlawfully?
a: John had told Herod it was unlawful for Herod to marry his brother’s wife.

q: How did Herod react when he heard John preach?
a: Herod became upset when he heard John preach, but he was still glad to hear him.

q: What oath did Herod swear to Herodias?
a: Herod swore that she could have whatever she asked of him, up to half of his kingdom.

q: For what did Herodias ask?
a: Herodias asked for the head of John the Baptizer on a platter.

q: How did Herod react to Herodias’ request?
a: Herod became very sorry but did not refuse her request, because of the oaths he had made in front of his guests.

q: What happened when Jesus and the apostles tried to go away by themselves to rest?
a: Many people recognized them and ran to arrive there before Jesus and the apostles.

q: What was Jesus’ attitude toward the crowd that was waiting for them?
a: Jesus had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd.

q: When asked by Jesus, what did the disciples think they would have to do to feed the people?
a: The disciples thought they would have to go and buy 200 denarii worth of bread.

q: What food did the disciples already have with them?
a: The disciples already had five loaves and two fish with them.

q: What did Jesus do as he took the loaves and fish?
a: As he took the loaves and fish, Jesus looked up to heaven, blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples.

q: How much food was left after everyone ate?
a: There were 12 baskets of bread, and pieces of fish left after everyone ate.

q: How many men had been fed?
a: There were 5,000 men that had been fed.

q: How did Jesus come to the disciples on the lake?
a: Jesus came to the disciples walking on the lake.

q: What did Jesus tell the disciples when they saw him?
a: Jesus told the disciples to be brave and to not be afraid.

q: Why did the disciples not understand about the miracle of the loaves?
a: The disciples did not understand about the miracle of the loaves because their minds were slow to understand.

q: What did the people of the region do when they recognized Jesus?
a: The people brought the sick on stretchers to Jesus wherever they heard he was coming.

q: What happened to those who just touched the fringe of Jesus’ garment?
a: Those who just touched the fringe of Jesus’ garment were healed.

q: What were some of Jesus’ disciples doing that offended the Pharisees and scribes?
a: Some of the disciples were eating with unwashed hands.

q: Whose tradition was it that hands, cups, pots, and copper vessels be washed before eating?
a: It was the tradition of the elders that hands, cups, pots, and copper vessels be washed before eating.

q: What did Jesus say to the Pharisees and scribes about their teaching on the issue of washing?
a: Jesus said that the Pharisees and scribes taught the rules of men while abandoning the commandment of God.

q: How did the Pharisees and scribes void the commandment of God which says to honor your father and mother?
a: They voided God’s commandment by telling people to give to them as Corban the money that would have helped their father and mother.

q: What did Jesus say does not defile a person?
a: Jesus said that nothing from outside of a person can defile him when it enters into him.

q: What did Jesus say defiles a person?
a: Jesus said that what comes out of a person defiles him.

q: What did Jesus say does not defile a person?
a: Jesus said that nothing from outside of a person can defile him when it enters into him.

q: What kinds of foods did Jesus declare to be clean?
a: Jesus declared all foods to be clean.

q: What did Jesus say defiles a person?
a: Jesus said that what comes out of a person defiles him.

q: What are three things that Jesus said can come out of a person to defile him?
a: Jesus said that evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery, coveting, wickedness, deceit, sensuality, envy, slander, pride, and folly can come out of a person to defile him.

q: Was the woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit a Jew or a Greek?
a: The woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit was a Greek.

q: How did the woman respond when Jesus told her that it was not right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs?
a: The woman said that even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.

q: What did Jesus do for the woman?
a: Jesus cast the demon out of the woman’s daughter.

q: When the man who was deaf and had a speech impediment was brought to Jesus, what did he do to heal him?
a: Jesus put his fingers in the man’s ears, spit and touched his tongue, then looked to heaven and said, “Open!”

q: What did the people do when Jesus told them to tell no one about his healings?
a: The more Jesus commanded them to be quiet, the more they talked about it.

q: What concern did Jesus state about the great crowd that had been following him?
a: Jesus stated that he was concerned the great crowd had nothing to eat.

q: How many loaves did the disciples have with them?
a: The disciples had seven loaves with them.

q: What did Jesus do with the disciples’ loaves?
a: Jesus gave thanks, broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to serve.

q: How much food remained after everyone had eaten?
a: There were seven baskets of food remaining after everyone had eaten.

q: How many people ate and were satisfied?
a: There were about 4,000 men who ate and were satisfied.

q: To test him, what did the Pharisees want Jesus to do?
a: The Pharisees wanted Jesus to give them a sign from heaven.

q: About what did Jesus warn his disciples concerning the Pharisees?
a: Jesus warned his disciples to be on guard against the yeast of the Pharisees.

q: About what did the disciples think Jesus was talking?
a: The disciples thought Jesus was talking about the fact that they had forgotten to bring bread.

q: Jesus reminded his disciples that what had happened when Jesus had broken five loaves?
a: Jesus reminded them that when he had broken five loaves, 5,000 people had been fed and 12 baskets full of broken pieces had been taken up.

q: What two things did Jesus first do to the blind man in order to restore his sight?
a: Jesus first spat on his eyes and laid his hands upon him.

q: What third thing did Jesus do to the blind man in order to completely restore his sight?
a: Jesus laid his hands upon his eyes again.

q: Who were the people saying that Jesus was?
a: The people were saying that Jesus was John the Baptizer, Elijah, or one of the prophets.

q: Who did Peter say that Jesus was?
a: Peter said that Jesus was the Christ.

q: About what future events did Jesus begin to teach his disciples clearly?
a: Jesus taught his disciples that the Son of Man must suffer, be rejected, be killed, and be raised after three days.

q: What did Jesus say when Peter began to rebuke him?
a: Jesus said to Peter, “Get behind me Satan! You do not care for the things of God, but for the things of people.”

q: What did Jesus say anyone who wants to follow him must do?
a: Jesus said that anyone who wants to follow him must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Jesus.

q: What did Jesus say about a person’s desire to gain the things of the world?
a: Jesus said, “What does it profit a person to gain the whole world and then forfeit his life?”

q: What did Jesus say he would do concerning those who are ashamed of him and his words?
a: Jesus said that at his coming he would be ashamed of those who were ashamed of him and his words.

q: Who did Jesus say would see the kingdom of God coming with power?
a: Jesus said that some standing there with him would not die before they saw the kingdom of God coming with power.

q: What happened to Jesus when Peter, James, and John went up a high mountain with him?
a: Jesus was transfigured and his garments became radiantly brilliant.

q: Who was talking with Jesus on the mountain?
a: Elijah and Moses were talking with Jesus.

q: On the mountain, what did the voice from the cloud say?
a: The voice said, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”

q: What did Jesus command the disciples about what they had seen on the mountain?
a: Jesus commanded them to tell no one what they had seen, until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.

q: What did Jesus say about Elijah’s coming?
a: Jesus said that Elijah does come first to restore all things, and that Elijah had already come.

q: What were the disciples unable to do for the father and his son?
a: The disciples were unable to drive out the evil spirit from the father’s son.

q: Into what did the evil spirit throw the boy to try to destroy him?
a: The evil spirit threw the boy into the fire or into the waters to try to destroy him.

q: How did the father respond when Jesus said all things are possible for the one who believes?
a: The father responded, “I believe! Help my unbelief!”

q: Why were the disciples unable to cast out the mute and deaf spirit in the boy?
a: The disciples were unable to cast out the spirit, because it could not be cast out except by prayer.

q: What did Jesus tell his disciples would happen to him?
a: Jesus told them he would be put to death, then after three days he would rise again.

q: What were the disciples arguing about along the way?
a: The disciples were arguing about who among them was the greatest.

q: Who did Jesus say is first?
a: Jesus said that he is first who is servant of all.

q: When someone receives a little child in Jesus’ name, who are they also receiving?
a: When someone receives a little child in Jesus’ name, they are also receiving Jesus and the one who sent Jesus.

q: What would be better for someone who causes a little one who believes in Jesus to stumble?
a: It would be better for that one if a millstone were tied around his neck and he was thrown into the sea.

q: What did Jesus say to do with your eye if it causes you to stumble?
a: Jesus said to tear out your eye if it causes you to stumble.

q: What did Jesus say happens in hell?
a: Jesus said that in hell the worm does not die, and the fire is not put out.

q: What question did the Pharisees ask Jesus in order to test him?
a: The Pharisees asked Jesus if it was lawful for a husband to divorce his wife.

q: What commandment had Moses given the Jews concerning divorce?
a: Moses had allowed a man to write a certificate of divorce and then send his wife away.

q: Why had Moses given the Jews this commandment concerning divorce?
a: Moses had given this commandment to the Jews because of their hard hearts.

q: To what event in history did Jesus refer when telling the Pharisees about God’s original design for marriage?
a: Jesus referred to the creation of male and female at the beginning when telling about God’s original design for marriage.

q: What did Jesus say the two people, the man and his wife, become when they are married?
a: Jesus said that the two become one flesh.

q: What did Jesus say about what God joins together in marriage?
a: Jesus said that what God joins together, let no man tear apart.

q: What was Jesus’ reaction when the disciples rebuked those bringing little children to him?
a: Jesus was angry with the disciples and told them to permit the little children to come to him.

q: How did Jesus say the kingdom of God must be received in order to enter it?
a: Jesus said the kingdom of God must be received as a little child in order to enter it.

q: What did Jesus first tell the man he must do to inherit eternal life?
a: Jesus told the man he must not kill, not commit adultery, not steal, not testify falsely, not defraud, and must honor his father and mother.

q: What additional commandment did Jesus then give the man?
a: Jesus then commanded the man to sell at that he had and to follow him.

q: How did the man react when Jesus gave him this commandment, and why?
a: The man was sorrowful and walked away, for he had many possessions.

q: Who did Jesus say had great difficulty entering the kingdom of God?
a: Jesus said that the rich had great difficulty entering the kingdom of God.

q: How did Jesus say even a rich person could be saved?
a: Jesus said that with people it is impossible, but with God all things are possible.

q: What did Jesus say anyone would receive who had left house, family, and lands for Jesus’ sake?
a: Jesus said they would receive a hundred times as much in this world, with persecutions, and eternal life in the world to come.

q: On what road were Jesus and the disciples traveling?
a: Jesus and the disciples were traveling on the road going up to Jerusalem.

q: What did Jesus tell his disciples would happen to him in Jerusalem?
a: Jesus told his disciples that he would be condemned to death and delivered over to the Gentiles.

q: What request did James and John make to Jesus?
a: James and John requested to sit on Jesus’ right and left hand with him in glory.

q: What did Jesus say that James and John would endure?
a: Jesus said that James and John would endure the cup Jesus would drink, and the baptism with which Jesus would be baptized.

q: Did Jesus grant the request of James and John?
a: No. Jesus said that the seats at his right and left hand were not his to give.

q: How did Jesus say the rulers of the Gentiles treat their subjects?
a: Jesus said that the rulers of the Gentiles dominate their subjects.

q: How did Jesus say those who wish to be great among the disciples must live?
a: Jesus said those who wish to be great among the disciples must be servant of all.

q: What did the blind man Bartimaeus do when many rebuked him, telling him to be quiet?
a: Bartimaeus cried out all the more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

q: What did Jesus say had healed Bartimaeus of his blindness?
a: Jesus said that Bartimaeus’ faith had healed him.

q: What did Jesus send two of his disciples to do in the village opposite them?
a: Jesus sent them to bring a colt to him that had never been ridden.

q: What happened when the disciples untied the colt?
a: Some people asked the disciples what they were doing, so they spoke to the people as Jesus told them, and the people let them go their way.

q: What did the people spread on the road as Jesus rode on the colt?
a: On the road the people spread their garments and branches they had cut from the fields.

q: What coming kingdom were the people shouting about as Jesus rode toward Jerusalem?
a: The people were shouting that the kingdom of their father David was coming.

q: What did Jesus do when he entered the temple area?
a: Jesus looked around and then went out to Bethany.

q: What did Jesus do when he saw the fig tree with no fruit on it?
a: Jesus said to the fig tree, “No one will ever eat fruit from you.”

q: What did Jesus do when he entered the temple area this time?
a: Jesus cast out the sellers and purchasers and would not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple.

q: What did Jesus say the temple was supposed to be, according to Scripture?
a: Jesus said that the temple was supposed to be a house of prayer for all the nations.

q: What did Jesus say the chief priests and scribes had made the temple?
a: Jesus said they had made the temple a den of robbers.

q: What were the chief priests and scribes trying to do to Jesus?
a: The chief priests and scribes were trying to kill Jesus.

q: What happened to the fig tree to which Jesus had spoken?
a: The fig tree to which Jesus had spoken withered away to its roots.

q: What did Jesus say about everything we ask for in prayer?
a: Jesus said that everything we ask for in prayer, believe that we have received it, and it will be ours.

q: What did Jesus say we must do so that the Father in heaven will also forgive you?
a: Jesus said we must forgive whatever we have against anyone so that the Father will also forgive us.

q: In the temple, what did the chief priests, scribes, and elders want to know from Jesus?
a: They wanted to know by what authority he did the things he was doing.

q: What question did Jesus ask the chief priests, scribes, and elders?
a: Jesus asked them if John’s baptism was from heaven or from men.

q: Why did the chief priests, scribes, and elders not want to answer that John’s baptism was from heaven?
a: They did not want to give this answer because Jesus would ask why they did not believe John.

q: Why did the chief priests, scribes, and elders not want to answer that John’s baptism was from men?
a: They did not want to give this answer because they feared the people, who all believed that John was a prophet.

q: After building and leasing the vineyard, what did the owner do?
a: After building and leasing the vineyard, the owner went away on a journey.

q: What did the vine dressers do to the many servants that the owner sent to receive the fruit of the vineyard?
a: The vine dressers beat some and killed some of the many servants.

q: Who did the owner send last to the vine dressers?
a: The owner sent his beloved son last.

q: What did the vine dressers do with the one sent last by the owner?
a: The vine dressers seized him, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.

q: What will the owner of the vineyard do to the vine dressers?
a: The owner of the vineyard will come and destroy the vine dressers and give the vineyard to others.

q: In the scripture, what happens to the stone which the builders rejected?
a: The stone which the builders rejected has been made the cornerstone.

q: What question did the Pharisees and some of the Herodians ask Jesus?
a: They asked him if it was lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not.

q: How did Jesus answer their question?
a: Jesus said they should give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s and give to God the things that are God’s.

q: In what did the Sadducees not believe?
a: The Sadducees did not believe in the resurrection.

q: In the story told by the Sadducees, how many husbands did the woman have?
a: The woman had seven husbands.

q: What question did the Sadducees ask Jesus about the woman?
a: They asked which of the men would be the woman’s husband in the resurrection.

q: What reason did Jesus give the Sadducees for their error?
a: Jesus said that the Sadducees did not know the scriptures nor the power of God.

q: What was Jesus’ answer to the Sadducees’ question about the woman?
a: Jesus said that in the resurrection, men and women will not marry, but will be like angels.

q: How did Jesus show from the scriptures that there is a resurrection?
a: Jesus quoted from the book of Moses, where God says that he is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, all whom must then be still alive.

q: What commandment did Jesus say is most important?
a: Jesus said that to love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, mind, and strength is the most important commandment.

q: What commandment did Jesus say is second?
a: Jesus said that to love your neighbor as yourself is the second commandment.

q: What question did Jesus ask about the Christ?
a: Jesus asked how David could call the Christ Lord when the Christ is the son of David.

q: What did Jesus tell the people to beware of concerning the scribes?
a: Jesus said that the scribes desire to be honored by men, but they devour widows’ houses and make long prayers for people to see.

q: Why did Jesus say that the poor widow had put in more than all who contributed to the offering box?
a: Jesus said she had contributed more because she gave out of her poverty while the others gave out of their abundance.

q: What did Jesus say would happen to the wonderful stones and buildings of the temple?
a: Jesus said that not one stone would be left on another.

q: What question did the disciples then ask Jesus?
a: The disciples asked Jesus when these things would happen, and what would be the sign.

q: About what did Jesus say the disciples must be careful?
a: Jesus said the disciples must be careful that no one lead them astray.

q: What did Jesus say would be the beginnings of birth pains?
a: Jesus said the beginning of birth pains would be wars, rumors of wars, earthquakes, and famines.

q: What did Jesus say would happen to the disciples?
a: Jesus said that the disciples would be delivered to councils, beaten in synagogues, and would stand before governors and kings as a testimony.

q: What did Jesus say must happen first?
a: Jesus said the gospel must be preached to all the nations first.

q: What did Jesus say would happen between family members?
a: Jesus said that one family member would deliver up another family member to death.

q: Who did Jesus say would be saved?
a: Jesus said that whoever endures to the end would be saved.

q: What did Jesus say those in Judea should do when they see the abomination of desolation?
a: Jesus said that those in Judea should flee to the mountains when they see the abomination of desolation.

q: What did Jesus say the Lord would do for the sake of the elect, so that they would be saved?
a: Jesus said the Lord would shorten the days of tribulation for the sake of the elect.

q: Who did Jesus say would arise to deceive people?
a: Jesus said that false Christs and false prophets would arise to deceive people.

q: What will happen to the lights and powers in the heavens after the tribulation of those days?
a: The sun and moon will be darkened, the stars will fall from the sky. The powers in the heavens will be shaken.

q: What will the people see in the clouds?
a: They will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.

q: What will the Son of Man do when he comes?
a: The Son of Man will gather his elect from the ends of the earth and the sky.

q: What did Jesus say would not pass away until all of these things occurred?
a: Jesus said that this generation would not pass away until all of these things occurred.

q: What did Jesus say would never pass away?
a: Jesus said that his words would never pass away.

q: When did Jesus say all these things would happen?
a: Jesus said that no one knows the day or hour except the Father.

q: What command did Jesus give his disciples regarding when the time is?
a: Jesus told his disciples to be alert, watch and pray.

q: What command did Jesus give his disciples regarding his coming?
a: Jesus told his disciples to be stay alert as they await his coming.

q: What command did Jesus give his disciples regarding his coming?
a: Jesus told his disciples to be alert and watch.

q: What were the chief priests and scribes considering how to do?
a: They were considering how to stealthily arrest Jesus and then kill him.

q: Why did the chief priests and scribes not want to act during the Feast of Unleavened Bread?
a: They were worried that a riot would arise among the people.

q: What did a woman do to Jesus at the house of Simon the leper?
a: A woman broke a vial of costly liquid and poured it on Jesus’ head.

q: For what were some rebuking the woman?
a: Some were rebuking the woman for not selling the perfume and giving the money to the poor.

q: What did Jesus say the woman had done for him?
a: Jesus said the woman had anointed his body for burial.

q: What promise did Jesus make about what the woman had done?
a: Jesus promised that wherever the gospel was preached in the whole world, what the woman had done would be spoken of in memory of her.

q: Why did Judas Iscariot go away to the chief priests?
a: Judas Iscariot went away to the chief priests so that he might deliver Jesus to them.

q: How did the disciples find the place where they would all eat the Passover?
a: Jesus told them to go into the city and follow a man carrying a pitcher of water, and then ask him where the guest room was that they would use to eat the Passover.

q: What did Jesus say as they were reclining at the table and eating?
a: Jesus said that one of the disciples eating with him would betray him.

q: Which disciple did Jesus say would betray him?
a: Jesus said that the disciple dipping bread with him in the bowl would betray him.

q: What did Jesus say about the destiny of the disciple who betrayed him?
a: Jesus said that it would have been better for him if he had not been born.

q: What did Jesus say as he gave the disciples the broken bread?
a: Jesus said, “Take this. This is my body.”

q: What did Jesus say as he gave the disciples the cup?
a: Jesus said, “This is my blood of the covenant, the blood that is poured out for many.”

q: When did Jesus say he would again drink of this fruit of the vine?
a: Jesus said he would again drink of this fruit of the vine on the day when he drank it anew in the kingdom of God.

q: At the Mount of Olives, what did Jesus predict about his disciples?
a: Jesus predicted that his disciples would all fall away because of him.

q: What did Jesus tell Peter after Peter said he would never fall away?
a: Jesus told Peter that before the rooster crowed twice, Peter would deny Jesus three times.

q: What did Jesus tell his three disciples to do while he prayed?
a: Jesus told them to remain there and watch.

q: For what did Jesus pray?
a: Jesus prayed that this hour might pass from him.

q: What was Jesus willing to accept as an answer to his prayer to the Father?
a: Jesus was willing to accept whatever the Father’s will was for him.

q: What did Jesus find when he returned to the three disciples?
a: Jesus found the three disciples sleeping.

q: What did Jesus find the second time he returned from praying?
a: Jesus found the three disciples sleeping.

q: What did Jesus find the third time he returned from praying?
a: Jesus found the three disciples sleeping.

q: What sign did Judas give to show the guards which person was Jesus?
a: Judas kissed Jesus to show which person was Jesus.

q: What did Jesus say was being done in his arrest to fulfill scripture?
a: Jesus said that scripture was being fulfilled because they came to arrest him like a robber, with swords and clubs.

q: What did those with Jesus do when Jesus was arrested?
a: Those with Jesus left him and fled.

q: What did a young man who was following Jesus do when Jesus was arrested?
a: The young man left his linen garment there and ran away naked.

q: Where was Peter as Jesus was taken to the high priest?
a: Peter sat among the guards, near a fire to keep warm.

q: What was wrong with the testimony against Jesus given to the Council?
a: The testimony against Jesus was false and did not agree.

q: What question did the high priest ask Jesus about who Jesus was?
a: The high priest asked Jesus if he was the Christ, the son of the Blessed.

q: What was Jesus’ answer to the high priest’s question?
a: Jesus answered by saying, “I am.”

q: Hearing Jesus’ answer, of what did the high priest say Jesus was guilty?
a: The high priest said that Jesus was guilty of blasphemy.

q: What did they do to Jesus after condemning him as one who deserved death?
a: They spit on him, struck him, and beat him.

q: What was Peter’s answer to the servant girl who said that Peter was with Jesus?
a: Peter answered that he did not know or understand about what the girl was talking.

q: What was Peter’s response when he was asked a third time if he was one of Jesus’ disciples?
a: Peter swore and put himself under curses that he did not know Jesus.

q: What happened after Peter answered the third time?
a: After Peter answered the third time, the rooster crowed a second time.

q: What did Peter do after he heard the rooster?
a: After he heard the rooster, Peter broke down and wept.

q: Early in the morning, what did the chief priests do with Jesus?
a: Early in the morning, they bound Jesus and handed him over to Pilate.

q: While the chief priests were presenting many charges against Jesus, what amazed Pilate about Jesus?
a: Pilate was amazed that Jesus no longer answered him.

q: What did Pilate usually do for the crowd at the time of the feast?
a: Pilate usually released to the crowd one prisoner they requested at the time of the feast.

q: Why did Pilate want to release Jesus to the crowd?
a: Pilate knew that it was because of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over to him.

q: Who did the crowd cry out to be released?
a: The crowd cried out for Barabbas to be released.

q: What did the crowd say should be done with the King of the Jews?
a: The crowd said that the King of the Jews should be crucified.

q: How did the cohort of soldiers dress Jesus?
a: The soldiers put a purple robe on Jesus and put on him a twisted crown of thorns.

q: Who carried Jesus’ cross?
a: A passerby, Simon of Cyrene, was forced to carry Jesus’ cross.

q: What was the name of the place where the soldiers brought Jesus to crucify him?
a: The name of the place was Golgotha, which means Place of a Skull.

q: What did the soldiers do with Jesus’ garments?
a: The soldiers cast lots for Jesus’ garments.

q: What charge against Jesus did the soldiers write on the sign?
a: The soldiers wrote “The King of the Jews” on the sign.

q: What did those who passed by challenge Jesus to do?
a: Those who passed by challenged Jesus to save himself and get down from the cross.

q: What did the chief priests say Jesus should do so they would believe?
a: The chief priests said that Jesus should come down from the cross so they would believe.

q: What titles did the chief priests use for Jesus as they mocked him?
a: The chief priests called Jesus the Christ and the King of Israel.

q: What happened at the sixth hour?
a: At the sixth hour, darkness came over the whole land.

q: What did Jesus cry out at the ninth hour?
a: Jesus cried out, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”

q: What did Jesus do before he died?
a: Jesus cried out with a loud voice before he died.

q: What happened in the temple when Jesus died?
a: The curtain of the temple was split in two from top to bottom when Jesus died.

q: What did the centurion testify when he saw how Jesus died?
a: The centurion testified that truly this man was the Son of God.

q: On what day did Jesus die?
a: Jesus died on the day before the Sabbath.

q: What did Joseph of Arimathea do after Jesus died?
a: Joseph of Arimathea took Jesus down from the cross, wrapped him in linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb, rolling a stone against the entrance of the tomb.

q: When did the women go to Jesus’ tomb to anoint his body?
a: The women went to the tomb on the first day of the week when the sun came up.

q: How did the women enter the tomb even though there had been a very large stone at the entrance?
a: Someone had rolled away the very large stone from the entrance.

q: What did the women see when they entered the tomb?
a: The women saw a young man dressed in a white robe sitting on the right side.

q: What did the young man say about Jesus?
a: The young man said that Jesus was risen and was not there.

q: Where did the young man say the disciples would meet Jesus?
a: The young man said the disciples would meet Jesus in Galilee.

q: To whom did Jesus first appear after his resurrection?
a: Jesus first appeared to Mary Magdalene.

q: How did Jesus’ disciples respond when Mary told them she had seen Jesus alive?
a: The disciples did not believe.

q: How did Jesus’ disciples respond when two other people told them they had seen Jesus alive?
a: The disciples did not believe.

q: When he appeared to the disciples, what did Jesus say to them about their unbelief?
a: Jesus rebuked the disciples for their unbelief.

q: What command did Jesus give the disciples?
a: Jesus commanded the disciples to go into all the world and preach the gospel.

q: Who did Jesus say would be saved?
a: Jesus said those who believed and were baptized would be saved.

q: Who did Jesus say would be condemned?
a: Jesus said those who did not believe would be condemned.

q: What signs did Jesus say would go with those who believed?
a: Jesus said those who believed would cast out demons, would speak in new languages, would not be hurt by anything deadly, and would heal others.

q: What happened to Jesus after he spoke to the disciples?
a: After he spoke to the disciples, Jesus was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.

q: What did the disciples then do?
a: The disciples then left and preached everywhere.

q: What did the Lord then do?
a: The Lord then worked with the disciples and confirmed the word with miraculous signs.
